environment: word-initially, between vowels and after a liquid
notes: '/h/ and /k/ are in complementary distribution: /h/ occurs in initial position, between V's and after liquids, whereas /k/ is the final C of a syllable' (§3.2); (h) is in parentheses in the chart.
'/h/ is not pronounced in medial position before /i/' (§3.2).

'/h/ occurs in initial and intervocalic position, and /k/ occurs in final position, as a component of a consonant cluster, and in initial position in lexemes if the next syllable begins with /h/' (§5.1).

notes: 'N + vl. stop or /s/ yields gemination of the latter ... geminated /s/ is realized as [ts]': hinsu [hitsu] (§3.3.1).
'The -/h/# sounds like German -ch ([x]); /h/- is usually not pronounced and is hardly ever distinctive in this position' (§1.3).
'/h/- is usually not pronounced' (§1.3): ayam/hayam, anat/hanat.
'In initial position /h/ is weak, and is often omitted, as in hasa: [hasa]=[asa]; but in some lexemes /h/ is never omitted, as in hakum' (§2.3).
